claims.text: The AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock is cobalt-free.
Conventionally bulk-fabricated AlCrFeNiSi tends to exhibit compositional segregation.
AlCrFeNiSi produced under standard, non-preheated LPBF conditions tends to exhibit compositional segregation.
AlCrFeNiSi produced under standard, non-preheated LPBF conditions tends to contain high residual thermal stresses.
AlCrFeNiSi produced under standard, non-preheated LPBF conditions tends to contain process-induced defects.
Laser additive manufacturing involves high cooling rates and temperature gradients.
Preheating the LPBF substrate to approximately 300–500 °C will reduce temperature gradients across deposited AlCrFeNiSi layers.
Elevating the substrate temperature will moderate the cooling rate of deposited AlCrFeNiSi.
A reduced temperature gradient will produce more uniform solidification.
More uniform solidification will reduce elemental segregation in AlCrFeNiSi.
Moderating the cooling rate will reduce thermal-contraction mismatch between successive LPBF layers.
Reducing temperature gradients and interlayer contraction mismatch will lower residual stresses.
Substrate preheating will improve metallurgical bonding in LPBF AlCrFeNiSi.
Substrate preheating will reduce defects such as microcracks and lack-of-fusion porosity.
Preheated specimens will have less grain-boundary compositional segregation than non-preheated LPBF or conventionally fabricated specimens.
Preheated LPBF AlCrFeNiSi specimens will have higher yield strength than the stated baselines.
Preheated LPBF AlCrFeNiSi specimens will have greater ductility than the stated baselines.
Excessively high substrate-preheat temperatures may cause grain coarsening or other adverse microstructural changes.
The proposed benefits apply under typical LPBF layer thicknesses and build atmospheres when the preheat temperature is optimized.

contradictions.description: The conditions specify that substrate preheating is the only processing change, but the baseline and predicted outcome also permit comparison with conventionally bulk-fabricated material. That comparison changes the fabrication route in addition to preheating and therefore is not the stated single-variable control.
